findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate()` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method added in this PR is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), and no no-arg overload exists in the super-class hierarchy (`UsernamePasswordForm` -> `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` -> `AbstractFormAuthenticator`). As written this is a compilation error and the `services` module (and therefore the whole build) will not compile. Either add the no-arg overload or pass `context.getUser()`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, disabling passkeys on the normal login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Both call sites use it to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`: `authenticate()` (line 115) and the error `challenge(context, error, field)` override (line 137). Before this change the condition was exactly the opposite (`context.getUser() == null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`), i.e. the webauthn/conditional-UI data was filled when the user had not yet been identified. `fillContextForm` is what sets the challenge auth note and the `enableWebAuthnConditionalUI`/challenge/rpId form attributes that the login template needs to render the `webauth` form and start conditional mediation. With the new condition, a first-time visitor (user == null) no longer gets any of that, so the primary ID-less passkey login (auto-login with a discoverable key, 'Sign in with passkey' link, passkey autofill on the username/password page) is silently removed, and the same happens on the error re-render after a bad username/password. Existing tests in all three Passkeys* test classes assert the presence of `//form[@id='webauth']` on the initial login page and auto-login with a discoverable key, so they will fail. The condition most likely needs to be 'passkeys enabled AND (user == null OR user has a passwordless webauthn credential)'.

findings.title: Overriding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to false removes the 'user has no passkey' guard during re-authentication
findings.body: `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm()` used the `user != null` branch not only to publish `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS`, but also to bail out (`return null`) when the identified user has no credential of the relevant type. By overriding `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` to always return `false` in the conditional-UI authenticator, that branch is never taken, so during re-authentication (where the user is already known) the passkey/conditional-UI markup is now injected unconditionally for every user in a passkeys-enabled realm, including users that have no passwordless WebAuthn credential at all. Combined with the `UsernameForm` change (which no longer skips the username form during re-authentication when passkeys are enabled), such users get an extra, useless screen with a passkey prompt, and any passkey they pick from the platform list that belongs to another account ends in a WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER error page. A check that the already-identified user actually has the passwordless credential configured is needed before enabling the conditional UI.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not test a user without a passkey
findings.body: The test name and the inline comment at line 304 ('Passkeys login should not be available on the page as this user does not have passkey') claim it covers re-authentication of a user that has no passkey, but the test sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, i.e. passkeys are disabled for the whole realm. The absence of the `webauth` form therefore proves nothing about per-user credentials. The actually interesting (and currently unverified) scenario introduced by this PR - passkeys enabled for the realm, user already identified for re-authentication but owning no passwordless WebAuthn credential - remains untested, which is exactly the path where the conditional UI is now shown unnecessarily. Either rename/retarget this test or add a second test with passkeys enabled and a user without a passkey credential.

findings.title: Overly broad try/catch(Exception) used to assert element absence
findings.body: The blocks at lines 291-296 and 312-317 call `driver.findElement(...)` inside `try { ...; fail(...); } catch (Exception nsee) { /* expected */ }`. Catching `Exception` swallows any WebDriver failure (e.g. TimeoutException, StaleElementReferenceException, WebDriverException from a broken page), so the assertion can pass for a completely unrelated reason and hide a real regression. The rest of the suite uses `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...))`; use that here so only the expected exception type satisfies the assertion.
